threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and responsibilities for the framework project.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Design and Rollout of Inclusive Hiring and Onboarding Framework project. Goal is to have a standardized, inclusive hiring and onboarding approach across business units within 30 days, using our current HRIS only.

Scope I am proposing:
- Map current hiring and onboarding flows across units and consolidate into a single process map linked to A1
- Standardize templates for job postings and interviews
- Define inclusive hiring and anti-bias guidance
- Create onboarding checklist and 90-day plan
- Define KPIs and reporting cadence, likely captured in A5 later

Out of scope for now:
- Implementing new HR tools or major HRIS changes
- Redesigning compensation structures

For ownership, I suggest:
- 17956 and 441030 co-own overall framework and tasks T1, T3, T5, T6, T8, T10, T12
- 167595, 549423, and 552174 focus on templates, onboarding, training, feedback and tasks T2, T4, T7, T9, T11

Can you all confirm if this scope and split works, or flag anything missing before we lock D1 and D2

Thanks for framing this. From a compliance and inclusion angle, the scope looks aligned with what we need.

Two clarifications before we confirm D1:
- Legal and employment law review: I can take the lead on ensuring T1, T3, T5, and T6 are compliant, but we will still need a formal review by our legal consultant before rollout.
- Accessibility: we should explicitly call out support for candidates and employees with disabilities in the process map A1 and in the onboarding checklist A3.

On ownership, I am comfortable co-owning the framework with you and taking primary responsibility for T1, T3, T5, T6, T8, T10, and T12, with you as co-owner on execution.

If no one objects, I would keep compensation and job grading fully out of scope for this project.

From the assistant side, the split makes sense to me.

For T2 and T4, I can start from our existing job ad and onboarding materials and align them to the new process map A1 once we have a first draft. I will also connect T2 with the inclusive guidance from T3 so that the templates already reflect anti-bias and accessibility points.

One question before we close D2: do you want a single point of contact per task, or can we list a primary and a backup for each assistant-owned task

Agree with the proposed scope and that we keep tools and compensation changes out for now.

I am happy to take primary ownership for T7, T9, and T11, with 552174 as backup if that works. For T7, I will make sure the manager training pack A6 is simple enough for non-HR managers and clearly linked to the new process.

On KPIs in T6, it would help if we define early which data we can realistically pull from HRIS so that A5 is feasible without manual work.

I can support on T2 and T4 as well, especially around drafting and formatting the templates and checklists.

For T11, I would like to help map the common issue types so that the escalation checklist A8 is practical for the HR team.

I do not see any missing items in the scope from my side.

Catching up on this thread now.

Scope looks ok to me. I just want to confirm that we will include steps for handling employee complaints during onboarding in A3 and in the process map A1, so that managers know when to involve HR.

I can support 17956 and 441030 on T1 and T6, especially around defining KPIs that reflect early retention and manager satisfaction.

On your question about ownership: I suggest we name a primary and a backup for each task so that we keep momentum even if someone is out.

Proposal:
- T2: primary 167595, backup 552174
- T4: primary 549423, backup 167595
- T7: primary 549423, backup 552174
- T9: primary 549423, backup 167595
- T11: primary 552174, backup 549423

If everyone is ok with this, we can lock D2.

The ownership proposal works for me. Having a backup per task will help with continuity.

For T2 and T4, I will coordinate with 549423 and 552174 so that we do not duplicate work on the templates and checklists.

Confirmed from my side on T4, T7, T9, and backup roles.

I will start by drafting a simple outline for A6 and a first pass at the onboarding checklist A3 so that we can validate the structure early.

I am ok with being primary on T11 and backup on T2 and T7.

Once we have the process map A1, I will draft the first version of the escalation checklist A8 and share it for review.

To close the loop on scope before we move on:
- In scope: process mapping T1, templates T2, inclusive guideline T3, onboarding checklist and 90-day plan T4, payroll and HRIS alignment T5, KPIs T6, manager training and communication T7, pilot T8, feedback T9, finalization T10, escalation path T11, and governance T12.
- Out of scope: new HR tools, major HRIS reconfiguration, compensation and grading redesign.

Unless there are objections today, I suggest we treat this as our agreed scope for D1.

Agree with the scope summary and the out-of-scope items.

On D2, we have now:
- Framework and governance (T1, T3, T5, T6, T8, T10, T12): 17956 and 441030
- Templates and onboarding (T2, T4, T7, T9, T11): 167595, 549423, 552174 with the primary/backup split described in M7.

If no one raises concerns, we can consider D2 confirmed and move on to drafting A1 and A4.
No concerns from me. The split is clear and I will support on T1 and T6 as needed, especially around the KPI definition and making sure the process map A1 is easy for managers to follow.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate standardized hiring templates and inclusive guidelines.

messages.text:
Sharing the first draft of the job posting and interview toolkit for the project.

For A4, I have included:
- Job posting template with sections for role summary, responsibilities, requirements, and a standard inclusion statement
- Guidance on inclusive language and avoiding biased phrasing, aligned with the upcoming guideline A2
- Structured interview guide with core questions and a simple scorecard for generic roles

This draft is linked to T2. I would like feedback from 17956 and 441030 on content, and from others on usability for managers. Once we align, we can move toward D3 for pilot approval.

Thanks for pulling this together.

Initial observations on A4:
- The inclusion statement is good, but we should explicitly mention equal opportunity, gender equality, and accommodations for candidates with disabilities.
- For the interview scorecard, we need a short note reminding managers to focus on job-related criteria only, to reduce bias.

In parallel, I have started drafting A2 for T3. It covers bias awareness, disability accommodations, and examples of compliant and non-compliant practices. I will share a link shortly so we can ensure A4 and A2 are fully aligned before we move to D3 and D4.

I went through the draft of A4.

From a manager usability perspective:
- The job posting template is clear, but we might want a short example posting appended so managers can see how it looks when filled in.
- The interview guide is solid. I suggest we add a short section on how to open and close interviews consistently, including a reminder to explain next steps and timelines.

Once A2 is shared, I will check that the examples in the guideline match the language in A4 so we do not confuse managers.

From the assistant side, I tested the job posting template with one of our recent roles.

A few practical suggestions for A4:
- Add a short checklist at the top for managers: confirm budget, confirm job grade, confirm hiring manager, etc.
- Include a field for preferred start date and whether the role is open to remote or hybrid work.

These small additions should help reduce back-and-forth with HR when managers submit requisitions.

I also reviewed the interview guide in A4.

One question: should we include any sample probing questions for each competency, or keep it generic for now and expand later after the pilot

I can help format the templates so they are easy to use in our current HRIS forms, as required by T2.

I like the structure of the job posting template.

Could we add a short note reminding managers to avoid internal jargon and acronyms in A4 so that candidates from different backgrounds can understand the role

Also, for the inclusive language section, maybe we can add a few do and do not examples to make it more concrete for managers who are not used to this.

I have now shared the draft of A2 for T3.

Key sections:
- Overview of fair and inclusive hiring principles
- Common bias types with examples
- Guidance on disability accommodations and how to handle requests
- Examples of compliant and non-compliant job postings and interview questions

Before we move to D4, I would like confirmation that the examples are realistic for our business units and that the guidance is understandable for non-HR managers.

I reviewed A2.

Strengths:
- The bias examples are concrete and easy to relate to.
- The section on disability accommodations is clear and gives managers practical steps.

Two small suggestions before we sign off D4:
- Add a short summary page at the start with key do and do not points.
- Include a reference to where managers can get legal support if they are unsure about a specific case.

Once these are in, I am comfortable treating A2 as ready for pilot use.

On probing questions in A4, my suggestion is to include 1–2 sample probes per competency now, but keep them generic enough so they work across roles. We can refine after T8 and T9 once we have pilot feedback.

I will also incorporate the checklist and remote/hybrid fields suggested by 549423, and the jargon note suggested by 82204.

I have updated A2 with:
- A one-page summary of key do and do not points
- A short section pointing managers to HR and our external legal consultant for complex cases

From a compliance and inclusion standpoint, I consider A2 fit for pilot. Unless there are strong objections today, I propose we treat this as sign-off for D4.

Thanks for iterating quickly on A4.

From my side, the template now:
- Covers inclusive language and clear structure
- Provides enough guidance for managers without overwhelming them

I suggest we approve A4 for pilot use under T2, with the understanding that we may refine it after T8 and T9. If no one disagrees, we can consider D3 confirmed.

No objections from me. A4 and A2 are clear enough for managers, and we can capture any confusion during the pilot.

I will incorporate the final versions into the manager training pack A6 under T7 so that managers see consistent examples.

I read through A2 and it is very clear. The examples of non-compliant questions are especially helpful.

I support using A2 and A4 in the pilot and will reinforce them when coaching managers on interviews.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize onboarding checklist, 90-day plan, and integration with payroll/HRIS.

messages.text:
I am sharing the first draft of the onboarding checklist and 90-day integration plan for A3, linked to T4.

Structure:
- Pre-boarding: contracts, equipment, system access, and any accommodations for people with disabilities
- First week: orientation, team introductions, mandatory trainings
- First month: role-specific training, early feedback touchpoints
- 90 days: performance and integration check-in, feedback from the new hire

I have tried to align the steps with the process map A1 and kept them compatible with our current HRIS and payroll processes. I would like feedback on feasibility, especially from 17956 and 441030 for HRIS/payroll touchpoints under T5.

Thanks for the draft.

From a process standpoint, A3 looks solid. A few points to check before we move toward D5 and D6:
- Payroll: we need to ensure that start dates, contract types, and cost centers are captured early enough so payroll can process without manual rework.
- HRIS: we should confirm that all mandatory fields in the system are covered by the checklist, especially for remote hires.

I will map the touchpoints for T5 and share a short summary of where onboarding steps intersect with payroll and HRIS.

I reviewed A3 with a focus on compliance and inclusion.

Suggestions:
- Pre-boarding: add a step to ask new hires if they need any workplace adjustments, with a clear contact point in HR.
- First week: include a short session on our code of conduct and anti-harassment policy.
- 90 days: ensure we capture feedback on whether the onboarding process supported their integration and any issues related to equality or accessibility.

On T5, I will work with 441030 to confirm that none of the new steps require changes to payroll calculations or new HRIS modules.

From a practical side, I checked A3 against a recent onboarding case.

The flow works, but I suggest we:
- Add a reminder for managers to schedule a 30-day and 60-day check-in, not only at 90 days.
- Include a simple checklist item for ensuring the new hire knows how to raise any concerns or complaints.

These additions should help with early retention and reduce escalations later.

I looked at the remote hire steps in A3.

Maybe we can:
- Add a specific section for remote onboarding: virtual introductions, equipment shipping, and remote access checks.
- Include a reminder to confirm time zone and preferred communication channels.

I can help adjust the checklist format so managers can easily tick items off in our existing tools.

I like the structure of the 90-day plan.

Could we add a short note for managers to check in on how well the role matches what was described during hiring This might help us catch any misalignment early and improve our templates A4 over time.

I have completed a quick mapping for T5.

Key touchpoints between A3 and payroll/HRIS:
- Pre-boarding: capture personal data, bank details, tax information, and cost center in HRIS before start date.
- First week: confirm attendance and any changes to working hours for payroll.
- 90 days: no direct payroll impact, but we may want to flag any contract changes.

The good news is that all of this can be handled with existing fields. We do not need new HRIS modules or manual spreadsheets.

Thanks for the mapping.

From a risk perspective, the main point is to avoid adding manual steps. Based on your summary, we are reusing existing HRIS and payroll fields, which is aligned with our constraints.

I suggest we document these touchpoints in A1 and A3 so managers and HR assistants see clearly where data must be entered or confirmed.

I have updated A3 with:
- A pre-boarding step to ask about workplace adjustments and provide an HR contact
- First week sessions on code of conduct and anti-harassment
- 30-day and 60-day check-ins, plus a note on how to raise concerns
- A dedicated section for remote onboarding, including time zone and communication preferences

Can we review this version and confirm if it is ready for pilot approval under D5

I reviewed the updated A3.

The checklist now:
- Covers pre-boarding, first week, first month, and 90 days
- Includes steps for people with disabilities and remote hires
- Aligns with our existing payroll and HRIS touchpoints from T5

From my side, I am comfortable approving A3 for pilot use. If 17956 agrees, we can treat this as confirmation of D5.

On D6, based on the mapping in M33 and our constraints:
- We are not introducing new payroll calculations or additional manual steps.
- We are only clarifying when data must be entered or confirmed in HRIS.

I therefore propose that we agree there are no required structural changes to payroll or HRIS for this framework. Any minor configuration tweaks will be handled within existing support processes.

Unless there are objections, we can consider D6 agreed.

No objections from me. A3 is clear and workable, and the HRIS and payroll touchpoints are straightforward.

I will support 549423 in preparing a short manager-facing version of the checklist for inclusion in A6 under T7.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and monitor the pilot, including training and communication to managers.

messages.text:
Proposing a plan for the pilot phase of the framework, linked to T8.

Suggested pilot business unit: Customer Support, because they have frequent hiring and a mix of on-site and remote roles.

Tentative timeline:
- Week 1: finalize A4, A2, and A3 for pilot; prepare manager training pack A6 under T7
- Week 2–4: run pilot in Customer Support, aiming to hire at least three roles using the new process
- Week 4–5: collect feedback under T9 and summarize in A7

We need to agree on D7 (business unit and timeframe) and D8 (manager communication and training plan). Feedback welcome before we confirm.

Customer Support is a good choice for the pilot. They have enough volume to test the framework and a variety of profiles, including part-time and remote roles.

On the timeline, I would just highlight that we need to leave room for legal review of the final templates and guidelines before we start the pilot. I can coordinate that in parallel during Week 1.

From my side, I am comfortable moving toward D7 with Customer Support and the proposed 4–5 week window, assuming we confirm manager availability for training.

For D8, here is a draft outline for the manager communication and training plan under T7 and A6:
- Kickoff email to Customer Support managers explaining the purpose of the pilot and what will change
- 60-minute virtual training session covering A1, A2, A3, and A4, with time for questions
- Quick reference guide summarizing key steps and responsibilities
- Follow-up reminder emails at the start and mid-point of the pilot

I can prepare the deck and quick reference guide and coordinate scheduling with the Customer Support lead.

I can support on T7 by drafting an FAQ section for A6 based on typical questions we get from managers, such as:
- How much extra time will the new process take
- What to do if a candidate requests an accommodation
- How to use the new interview scorecard

This should help reduce confusion during the pilot.

For T9, I suggest we prepare a short survey for managers and candidates in Customer Support.

We can ask about:
- Clarity of job postings A4
- Experience with interviews and fairness
- Onboarding experience using A3

I can help set up the survey and track responses so we can build A7 at the end of the pilot.

Customer Support seems like a good test area.

One concern: their managers are already quite busy. We should keep the training session focused and maybe offer a recording for those who cannot attend live.

Also, can we clarify how we will handle exceptions during the pilot, for example urgent hires that cannot follow every step of the new process

Good point on manager time.

For D8, I propose we:
- Keep the live training to 60 minutes max
- Provide a recording and the quick reference guide
- Offer optional 15-minute office hours during the first two weeks of the pilot

For exceptions, we can define a simple rule in A6: urgent hires can skip some steps with HR approval, but must still use the inclusive templates A4 and follow the minimum onboarding steps in A3.

On D7, I confirm my support for:
- Business unit: Customer Support
- Timeframe: 4–5 weeks as outlined, with Week 1 for finalization and training, Weeks 2–4 for active pilot, and Week 4–5 for feedback and analysis under T9.

I will inform the Customer Support lead and ensure they are aligned with the plan and expectations.

I will adjust A6 to reflect:
- A 60-minute live session with recording
- Quick reference guide and FAQ
- Optional office hours during the first two weeks
- Clear rules for urgent exceptions, as you described

Once updated, I believe the communication and training plan under T7 will be ready for D8.

I reviewed the updated A6.

The plan is clear, concise, and realistic for Customer Support managers. It explains what is changing, what managers need to do, and where to get help.

From my side, I am comfortable approving the manager communication and training plan for the pilot. Unless there are objections, we can treat this as confirmation of D8.
No objections from me. I will support during the pilot by helping managers with any questions on A4 and A3 and by collecting qualitative feedback for T9 and A7.
I will start drafting the survey questions for T9 this week and share a preview so we can confirm they align with the pilot goals and the content of A2, A3, and A4.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot feedback, agree on adjustments, and confirm final rollout plan.

messages.text:
We have completed the pilot in Customer Support and compiled the feedback into A7, linked to T9 and T10.

Key themes from managers and candidates:
- Job postings A4 were clearer and more inclusive, but some managers felt the template was slightly long.
- Interview guides and scorecards were appreciated, though a few managers asked for more role-specific examples.
- Onboarding checklist A3 helped structure the first weeks, but some steps were not consistently followed by line managers.

We now need to agree on which changes to make to the framework for D9 and confirm the go-live date and governance approach for D10.

Looking at A7, I would suggest the following adjustments for D9:
- A4: create a short version of the job posting template for simple roles, while keeping the full version for more complex positions.
- A3: highlight the must-do steps versus nice-to-have items, so managers know where to focus if they are short on time.

These changes should address the main concerns without diluting the framework.

From the survey results in A7, candidates appreciated the clarity on next steps during onboarding, but some mentioned delays in receiving equipment for remote roles.

Maybe we can:
- Strengthen the pre-boarding section in A3 to include clear deadlines for equipment requests.
- Add a KPI in A5 under T6 to track completion of key onboarding steps, such as equipment readiness on day one.

I noticed in A7 that some managers still felt unsure about how to handle accommodation requests.

Maybe we should:
- Add a short reminder in A6 pointing them back to the relevant section in A2.
- Include a contact list in A8 so they know exactly who to reach out to when they are not sure.

From an overall perspective, the pilot results in A7 are positive: better candidate experience and more structured onboarding, with some adoption gaps.

For D9, I propose we agree on this list of framework changes:
- Introduce a short version of A4 for simple roles.
- Mark must-do steps in A3 and reinforce pre-boarding equipment deadlines.
- Add a KPI in A5 to track completion of key onboarding steps.
- Update A6 and A8 to make support contacts and accommodation guidance more visible.

If we align on this list, we can proceed with T10 to update all affected artifacts.

I agree with the proposed list of changes for D9.

From a compliance and inclusion standpoint, these adjustments strengthen the framework without adding unnecessary complexity. I will also double-check that the new KPI in A5 does not require data we cannot reliably capture from HRIS.

Once we confirm D9, we can set a realistic go-live date and define the governance cycle under T12.

I will take the lead on T10 to implement the agreed changes:
- Create the short version of A4.
- Update A3 with must-do markers and clearer equipment deadlines.
- Work with 17956 to add the onboarding completion KPI to A5.
- Update A6 and support 552174 on A8.

I will share updated drafts for review before we announce the final framework.

I will update A8 under T11 to include:
- Clear contact points for HR, legal, and IT support
- A simple escalation flow for hiring and onboarding issues

This should make it easier for managers and HR assistants to route issues quickly.

On D10, I propose the following:
- Go-live date: two weeks from today, to allow time to finalize updates under T10 and T11 and communicate to all business units.
- Governance model under T12:
  - 17956 as overall owner of the framework.
  - Quarterly review of A1–A8, using data from A5 and feedback from HR and managers.
  - Change log maintained centrally so updates are transparent.

If everyone is comfortable with this, we can confirm D10 and close T12.

The go-live date and governance approach work for me.

I will support by gathering feedback after the first quarter and summarizing key themes so we can feed them into the next review cycle under T12.

No concerns from my side. The quarterly review and clear ownership should help keep the framework current without constant changes.

I will help communicate the go-live date and key changes to managers in my area.
